info.title: Taba client API
info.description:
The API that applications and `taba-cli` use, on `api.port` (default 8080): topics, messages (publish, consume, invisibility, confirm, prune), tokens, who the caller is, the nodes, the statistics and, for an `admin` token, the cluster. A route's `Permission` is in its description; each one applies only with authentication on. Errors are always an `ErrorResponse`, and every response carries `X-Request-Id`.

The monitoring API (`/health/*`, `/metrics`, `/metrics/topics*` without a token, for the collectors inside the infrastructure) is a separate document, served on `operations.port`.

get.summary:
Who the token is and what it can do, so a client can enable or disable what it shows before calling. With
authentication off everyone is the `open` caller, with every permission.
get.description: Permission: any valid token. It is exempt from the rate limit.

401.description: `auth.unauthorized`: the token is missing, malformed, unknown, revoked or expired. Only with authentication on.

403.description:
`auth.forbidden` (the token lacks the permission; `required` says which) or `auth.out-of-scope` (the topic is
outside the token's prefixes).

post.summary:
Sends the memory and the disk of **every** node to the S3 bucket, without stopping anything. The node that receives
it forwards to the others and joins the answers. In the client API it asks for a token; on the monitoring port the
same route has none.

200.description: `complete` says if nothing was left pending, and `nodes` has the report of each node.

post.summary:
Declares the cluster restored from disk with the nodes that are present: the FIFO queues are released and a
restoration held by the strict mode goes on. It is spread to every node. **Messages already consumed may
reappear.** It is what releases a cluster stuck by the loss of two nodes.

post.summary:
Stops the whole cluster: it drains every node and, with S3, writes the list of the nodes that were alive. The
processes keep running as `drained`: stopping them is up to the orchestrator.

get.summary:
The process is up and answering. If it fails, the orchestrator restarts the process. It needs no token, on either
port, because the probe of an orchestrator cannot send one.

The node is **able to receive traffic**: registered, synchronization finished, outside bootstrap and return. In drain
it answers `503`. It never answers with an `ErrorResponse`: the body is always a `HealthResponse`, so the
orchestrator can read the reason. It needs no token, on either port.

The metrics of **this node**, in Prometheus text (`Accept: application/openmetrics-text` asks for OpenMetrics). One
target per node: the node does not query the others. The route does not exist (`404`) with
`telemetry.prometheus.enabled` off.
get.description:
**Authentication depends on the port.** On the monitoring port (`operations.port`) it needs no token, for the
collectors inside the infrastructure. On the client port it takes **any valid token**, no particular permission,
because that port is reachable from outside. A node in drain only validates the root token.

200.description: The metrics, as text: Prometheus (`text/plain; version=0.0.4`) or, if the `Accept` header asks for `application/openmetrics-text`, OpenMetrics.

get.summary:
Who is in the cluster and in what state, without addresses. A node that does not answer shows up with
`reachable: false` and the state the member table has; a node that left by drain shows up as `drained`, in the
answer of any node. The numbers are consolidated across the cluster (`partial` and `missingNodes` say if some node
did not answer within 5 seconds).

without waiting to fill `maxMessages` (with `waitTime` above 0 it waits only for the first one). Any `GET` counts as
a consumer for the idleness of a volatile queue.

parameters.description: Create the queue if it does not exist. The next parameters only apply at creation.

post.summary:
Publishes a message. The body is the **bytes** of the message and `Content-Type` says what they are (without it,
`application/json`); Taba stores the bytes as they came. `application/json` must be valid JSON and `text/*` valid
UTF-8. The node that receives is the coordinator and answers when the quorum confirms.
post.description:
On a queue the answer is `201` with the `id` (on a FIFO queue, `200` with `duplicate: true` when the publication
repeated one inside the deduplication window); on a distributor it is `200` with what happened to each destination
queue.

Permission: `publish`. On a distributor only it is checked, not the destination queues.

parameters.name: groupId
parameters.description: Group (1 to 128 characters of `A-Za-z0-9_-.:`). Required on a FIFO queue; elsewhere it guides the fair delivery.

parameters.name: deduplicationId
parameters.description: FIFO queues only: the deduplication key inside the group (default: the SHA-256 of the body). Elsewhere it is `400 validation.not-applicable`.

requestBody.description: The message bytes, of any media type up to the topic's `maxMessageBytes` (default 5 MB).

200.description: A duplicate on a FIFO queue, or the result of a distributor.

ClusterStatus.description: The state and the conditions of the cluster.

scope.description: `cluster` (asks every node) or `node` (only the one that answers).

worstCondition.description: The condition of highest severity; `ok` if none.

ClusterStatusNode.description: One node in the cluster status.

oneOf.description: `null` if the node did not answer.

members.description: How many members are in each state.

plannedStop.description: `true` if the stop was `POST /cluster/stop` (it left a stop list in S3).

servingNodes.description: Nodes that are active and out of drain.

stopped.description: `true` if every node that answered is in drain.

ConsumeResponse.description:
`ConsumeResponse`: serialized directly, so the JSON `body` does not go through a `Value` and lose
the form in which it was sent.

messages.description: Empty when nothing was ready: the answer is then `200`, never `204`.

DeliveryError.description: Why a copy of a message to one destination queue failed.

DistributorDelivery.description: What happened to one destination queue of a distributor: `id` (a copy was created) or `error`.

DistributorPublishResponse.description: Answer of a publication to a distributor. Zero matches is not an error.

matched.description: Queues whose name matched a prefix.

DistributorStats.description: What a distributor received and copied.

pendingMessages.description: Messages still in memory that the drain has to move.

trigger.description: What started the drain: `api` or `signal`; `null` when there is none.

ErrorDetail.description: A specific problem inside a validation error (`details`).

field.description: The field the problem is in (`name`, `permissions[1]`, `query.limit`...).

ErrorResponse.description: Body of every error response (`4xx` and `5xx`) of a JSON route.

code.description:
A stable code of the catalogue, in the `group.reason` format. A client must tolerate codes it does not
know yet: the catalogue only grows.

details.description: What is wrong in each field, on a validation error.

requestId.description: The same value as the `X-Request-Id` header of the response.

required.description: On a `403 auth.forbidden`: what the token lacked, `root` or the name of a permission.

GroupStats.description: The numbers of one group (`groupId`) of a topic.

overflow.description: `true` for the row that sums the groups past the ceiling.

share.description: The fraction of the topic's messages that are in the group.

HealthResponse.description:
Body of `/health/live` and `/health/ready`. These routes never return an `ErrorResponse`
(doc 06b), so the orchestrator can read the reason without handling errors.

Latency.description: Latency percentiles, in seconds; `null` with no observation.

Me.description: Who the caller is and what it can do.

root.description: `true` for the root token and, with authentication off, for everyone.

body.description:
What was published, according to `contentType`: the native JSON for `application/json` (or `*/*+json`), a
string for `text/*` in UTF-8, and the bytes in base64 for any other type (then `bodyEncoding` is `base64`).

bodyEncoding.description: `base64`, when the body is not JSON nor text.

deliveryCount.description: Deliveries so far, this one included.

invisibleUntil.description: The end of the invisibility of this delivery.

receiptToken.description: Keep it: it is required to confirm the message and to change its invisibility.

MessageBytes.description: The bytes of a message, of any media type: the request body of a publication.

MissingNode.description: A node that did not answer a consolidated read.

Node.description: One member of the cluster. There are no addresses.

partial.description: `true` if some node did not answer in time (the numbers are those of the ones that did).

NodeRuntime.description: What a node's registry says about its load.

channelRttP95Seconds.description: The worst `p95` of the round trip of the node's channels; `null` with no observation.

rateLimitRejected.description: Requests refused with `429` since the start.

signals.description: The raw signals the conditions come from.

PruneNode.description: What each node removed in a prune.

pruneId.description: Identifies the operation; it makes the call idempotent on each node.

removed.description: Messages removed, each counted once (the node that owns a message counts it, the replicas do not).

PublishOutcome.description: What a publication answers with `200`: a duplicate on a FIFO queue, or the result of a distributor.

PublishResponse.description: Answer of a publication to a queue.

duplicate.description:
FIFO queues only: `true` if the publication repeated one inside the deduplication window (nothing was
created; the status is then `200`).

id.description: The message `id`; on a duplicate, the one of the original.

StopReport.description: What the stop of the whole cluster did.

nodes.description: One entry per node: `nodeId`, `drained` and, if it failed, `error`.

stopList.description: `true` if the stop list was written to S3.

Token.description: An access token, without its secret.

permissions.description: At least one. An `admin` token is only created by the root token.

topicPrefixes.description: Empty or absent means every topic.

TokenCreated.description: The creation of a token: the `Token` plus its secret, which shows up **only here**.

TokenUpdateRequest.description: Body of `PATCH /tokens/{id}`. Permissions and prefixes are immutable.

expiresAt.description: A date in the future; `null` removes the deadline.

Topic.description: A topic: a queue (with its dead-letter queue) or a distributor.

deadLetter.description: Only on a dead-letter queue, where it is `true`. A dead-letter queue is read-only and follows its source.

oneOf.description: Queue only: the values that apply.

idleTimeout.description: Volatile queue only: seconds without a consumer until the queue is deleted.

maxDeliveries.description: Queue only: `null` means the node default (10).

maxMessageBytes.description: Queue only: `null` means the node default (`message.max-bytes`).

source.description: Only on a dead-letter queue: the name of the queue it belongs to.

tags.description: Telemetry tags; they do not change the behaviour.

ttl.description: Queue only: `null` means the node default (14 days).

TopicCondition.description: A condition found on a topic.

TopicCreateRequest.description: Body of `POST /topics`. A field that does not apply to the type is `400 validation.not-applicable`.

fifo.description: Queue only. Immutable. Needs `replication.factor` of at least 2.

idleTimeout.description: Volatile queue only: 60 to 604800 seconds. Default 600.

name.description: `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,100}$`. A name ending in `-dead-letter` is reserved.

prefixes.description: Distributor only: up to 20 prefixes of 1 to 100 characters (`A-Za-z0-9_-`).

tags.description: Up to 20 tags: key of 1 to 64 and value of 0 to 128 characters of `A-Za-z0-9_-.:`.

TopicEffective.description: The limits in force for a queue: its own value, or the node default where it has none.

maxDeliveries.description: Deliveries without an ack until the message goes to the dead-letter queue.

nextCursor.description: Absent on the last page; pass it as `cursor` to read the next one.

TopicStats.description: The numbers of a topic. With `fields`, only the requested ones come (`id` and `name` always do).

depth.description: Messages in the queue, visible and invisible.

partial.description: Only in the client API: some node did not answer, so the numbers are those of the ones that did.

topGroups.description: Only on the detail of one topic: up to `stats.topics.top-groups` (default 10) groups, largest first.

TopicStatsGroup.description: With `groupBy`, one row per value of the tag: the sums of the topics that have that value.

tag.description: The tag the rows are grouped by.

topics.description: How many topics have that value.

value.description: The value of the tag in this row.

TopicStatsPage.description: A page of topic numbers (or, with `groupBy`, of rows per tag value).

TopicStatsRow.description: An item of a page of topic numbers: a topic, or, with `groupBy`, a row per tag value.

TopicUpdateRequest.description:
Body of `PATCH /topics/{topic}`: only what is sent changes. `tags` replaces the whole map, and `null` in
`maxMessageBytes`, `ttl` or `maxDeliveries` goes back to the node default. `name`, `id`, `type`, `volatile` and
`fifo` are immutable: sending them, even with the current value, is `400 validation.immutable-field`.

visibilityTimeout.description:
The new invisibility, in seconds **from now** (not an increment). `0` releases the message at once. At most
`delivery.visibility-timeout.max`.

invisibleUntil.description: The end of the invisibility; with `0`, the current instant.

bearer.description: `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. A node that has neither a root token nor `auth.dev-token` runs with authentication off and takes no token.

tags.name: Messages
tags.description: Publish, consume, change the invisibility, confirm and prune.

tags.name: Tokens
tags.description: Access tokens. Only with authentication on.

tags.name: Statistics
tags.description: The numbers of the topics, for the whole cluster.

tags.name: Cluster
tags.description: The nodes and the cluster (`admin` permission).

tags.name: Health
tags.description: The probes of the orchestrator. They take no token.

tags.name: Metrics
tags.description: This node's Prometheus metrics, behind a token on this port.
